events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Delta Junction; Tanana Flats; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Wintry mix. Total snow accumulations up to two inches.

* WHERE...Chatanika River Valley, Delta Junction, Eielson AFB,
Salcha, Fairbanks Metro Area, Goldstream Valley, Nenana Hills,
Tanana Flats, and Two Rivers.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Multiple fronts are expected to move over the
area on Sunday and Monday, both of which are expected to bring a
wintry mix. Precipitation will change to mostly rain during the
overnight hours Sunday into Monday. A portion of the rain that
falls may freeze on contact with below freezing surfaces before
warming temperatures limit freezing.

16 inches. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...South Slopes of the Central Brooks Range.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The snow will come in two waves. Snow is

and continues into the evening with an additional 4 to 8 inches of
snow.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 and
12 inches and a glaze of ice. Winds gusting as high as 30 mph.

* WHERE...Upper Koyukuk Valley.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The snow will come in two waves. Snow is
expected to continue into Sunday morning with 3 to 6 inches of
total snow expected. There will be a break with lighter snow Sunday
afternoon and night. On Monday, snow is likely in the morning with
2 to 4 inches expected but rain becomes more likely in the
afternoon as temperatures warm. A portion of the rain that falls
may freeze on contact with below freezing surfaces before warming
temperatures limit freezing.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Francisco Bay, Monterey
Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
11:07 AM Sunday 10/25, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
11:39 AM Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at
12:15 PM Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at
12:56 PM Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft
MLLW) at 01:43 PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up
to 1.0 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
